items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: "I'd love to have a boom-ch, oom-ch, oom-ch-boom job with Guy Lombardo and make a million dollars a year and just go out and get me some kicks."

ctx.x: I shudder to think of what he is now.

Because you must remember that Buddy's standing on the stage like a Sammy Davis Jr., he has watched. He's absorbed like a sponge. He's gotten there. (SHORT SILENCE HERE.) ...It would cost a whole lot of money. It will cost more than Guy Lombardo. But I would shudder to think, had he got from the time he was about 20, 19 or 20 years old, had he been allowed the privilege to play like with the Basie band or like to play with the Lunceford band. Who could tell? Gene Krupa was denied that privilege. Gene used to…

You see, these great drummers—this is this game I wanted to play—they seem to have done what you say... Because of all of these great drummers, I'll name the drummer and you name the band, because all of these bands happen to turn out to be famous bands. We'll start with some white drummers. Cliff Leeman. What band, Jo?
